launch-desk.sentence: Aurelith launched the Visor on Monday, its first mixed-reality headset.
At launch, it will only be sold in the US and Canada.

byteward.sentence: Aurelith on Monday introduced the Visor, the company's first mixed-reality headset.
Each eye gets its own 3,400 by 3,400 pixel display.
Aurelith rates the battery for 2.5 hours of use.
The Visor's app store will open with 320 apps.

frametime.sentence: Aurelith's first mixed-reality headset, the Visor, launched today.
In our testing, 10 of the 12 games we tried held a steady 90 frames per second.
The toughest, Glasshollow, averaged 71 fps at high settings.
Aurelith quotes 2.5 hours of battery life.
In our gaming runs, the battery lasted 2 hours and 10 minutes.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: Aurelith has unveiled the Visor, its first mixed-reality headset.
The battery rides in a separate 210 g pack on a cable.
Behind the lenses sit two 3,400 by 3,400 pixel displays, one per eye.
The field of view is 100° horizontally.
Apps never see raw eye-tracking data, only the moment the wearer confirms a selection.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Aurelith released the Visor, its first mixed-reality headset, on Monday.
Aurelith says raw eye-tracking data is processed on the headset and never sent to its servers.
Apps get only the wearer's selections, not the gaze data itself, under the company's developer terms.
A pending bill, the Gaze Data Privacy Act, would ban the sale of eye-tracking data.
Companies that break it would face fines of up to $7,500 per affected user.
